description: Half-Stack Developers brings together two National University of Singapore students with interests in software engineering, AI and data science, united by a curiosity about our changing planet. Through Trend Detective, we aim to make NASA Earth observation data accessible and help people explore environmental trends with clear, evidence-based explanations.
summary: Half-Stack Developers presents Trend Detective, an educational application that helps students and the public investigate environmental change using NASA Earth science data. Users select a location, variable and time period to explore interactive charts, compare places and estimate rates of change. Powered by NASA POWER data, each investigation becomes an inspectable case file containing visualisations, source information, limitations and downloadable evidence. For eligible annual temperature records, the app evaluates statistical significance under documented assumptions; other variables, seasonal analyses and comparisons remain descriptive. Our detective-inspired interface and interpretation lesson help users distinguish a trend’s size from the strength of its evidence and understand why historical trends alone cannot establish causation or predict the future. An OpenAI-powered RAG assistant supports natural-language investigation planning and explanations grounded in NASA documentation and reviewed project methodology. The assistant is enabled in our local demo but remains experimental; users confirm proposed settings, and numerical analysis stays in Python. Our goal is to make environmental evidence accessible, transparent and reproducible.
details:
1. WHAT TREND DETECTIVE DOES

Is an environmental change a lasting trend, or could it reflect ordinary variability? Half-Stack Developers built Trend Detective to help students and the public investigate this question using NASA Earth science data.

The application connects variable selection, regional data access, time-series visualisation and statistical interpretation in one detective-inspired experience. Each investigation becomes a case file containing charts, estimated rates of change, applicable statistical evidence, source information and downloadable values.

Users can explore temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind and soil wetness, compare places and inspect the evidence behind each conclusion. Our intended audience includes high-school and college students and interested members of the public.

2. HOW IT WORKS

  1. Ask and confirm: In our AI-enabled demo, users describe an environmental question and review the assistant’s proposed variable, location and period. Manual settings and saved examples remain available.
  2. Obtain NASA data: The backend retrieves monthly NASA POWER records through a dedicated source adapter and cache. Evidence identifies the requested location and the actual geographic grid cell.
  3. Analyse consistently: Python preserves missing values, calculates calendar-day-weighted summaries and estimates Sen’s rate of change. Missing observations are never replaced by zero.
  4. Inspect the result: Interactive charts show historical patterns, estimated rates and statistical evidence where supported.
  5. Ask and learn: Users ask the assistant about datasets, methods and limitations, inspect its citations, compare places over common complete years and complete an interpretation lesson.
  6. Reproduce and share: Users download CSV values and PNG charts, inspect retained evidence and share pinned investigation links. Replaying a pinned case requires the application to retain its supporting snapshots.

3. KEY TECHNICAL AND CREATIVE CONTRIBUTIONS

An evidence-centred detective experience
Trend Detective brings analysis, interpretation and verification into one case file. Variable definitions, units, geographic context, methods and limitations accompany each result, helping users follow the evidence behind a conclusion. An interpretation lesson addresses three common misunderstandings: a large trend is different from strong statistical evidence; non-significance does not prove an absence of change; and a historical trend alone cannot establish causation or predict the future.

Statistical analysis with an explicit scope
Sen’s slope estimates change in the variable’s units per decade. Formal significance testing is restricted to eligible annual two-metre air-temperature records containing 20–45 contiguous complete years, under our documented Mann–Kendall-based, Monte Carlo inference policy. Simulation checks examine behaviour under specified serial-dependence assumptions, while other variables, seasonal analyses, maps and place comparisons remain descriptive. We withhold unsupported p-values and confidence intervals, and all numerical results and statistical verdicts come from deterministic Python code.

An assistant grounded in documentation
We implemented and evaluated an experimental OpenAI-powered retrieval-augmented generation pipeline for natural-language investigation planning and qualitative explanations. Planning translates questions into proposed settings for user confirmation, while RAG retrieves relevant passages from 173 reviewed text sections covering 13 NASA sources and 10 project method/variable notes. Responses are checked for citations, allowed result references and consistency with the investigation; the LLM does not calculate statistics or replace canonical verdicts. The assistant is enabled in our local demo but remains experimental because explanation quality has not yet met our release target. The manual investigation workflow operates independently.

4. TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

The prototype runs locally without downloading a language model. The assistant uses OpenAI-hosted services, with credentials kept on the backend and configurable usage limits.

5. INTENDED IMPACT AND NEXT STEPS

Trend Detective aims to help learners move from seeing a graph to asking better questions: What changed? Over which years? What does this variable represent? How strong is the evidence? What remains unknown?

By connecting exploration, evidence and interpretation, we aim to make environmental investigation more accessible and reproducible. Students and educators could use its case files as starting points for discussions about environmental change and responsible statistical reasoning.

Next steps include improving source-grounded explanations, further technical review, observing intended users and verifying public deployment. User testing has not been conducted, so improved learning outcomes remain an intended benefit rather than a measured result.
